result.topic_en: Calculations on the potential of two spheres (bispherical/toroidal-type coordinates): reduction of Laplace's equation to a hypergeometric equation, solution via Riemann P-functions, and evaluation of a related definite integral as series of Gamma-function (Π) quotients.
result.transcription:
Potential zweier Kugeln Februar 1856.

$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial r^2}+\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}+\frac{1}{rr}\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \varphi^2}=0$
$u=v\,r^{-\frac12}$
$r\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial r}r^{+\frac12}-\frac12 v\,r^{-\frac12}$
$\frac{\partial r\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}}{r\partial r}=\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial r^2}r^{-\frac12}+\frac14 v\,r^{-\frac52}$
$rr\left(\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial r^2}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}\right)+\left(\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial \varphi^2}+\frac14 v\right)=0$
$\frac{\partial v}{\partial z}=\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial r}-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}i\right)\frac12$
$\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial z\partial z'}=\left(\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial r^2}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}\right)\frac14$
$\frac12(z+z')^2\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial z\partial z'}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial \varphi^2}+\frac14 v=0$

$r+xi=z$
$r-xi=z'$
$r=\frac{z+z'}{2}\quad xi=\frac{z-z'}{2}$

[-$=$-] $r=\varrho\cos\psi$

$z^{\mu}z'^{\mu'}$

$(\cos\psi)^2\left(\frac{\partial^2 v}{(\partial\log\varrho)^2}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\psi^2}\right)+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\varphi^2}+\frac14 v=0$

$\cos\psi=x$

$\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\psi^2}=-\frac{\partial\sin\psi\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}}{\partial\psi}=+\sin\psi^2\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}-\cos\psi\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}$

$2(1+x)\left((1-x^2)\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}-x\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{(\partial\log\varrho)^2}\right)+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\varphi^2}+\frac14 v=0$
$1+x=y$
$2y^2(2-y)\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial y^2}+2y(1-y)\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}+2y\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\log\varrho^2}+\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial\varphi^2}+\frac14 v=0$

$\frac{1+\cos 2\psi}{2}$

$y^2(1-y)\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial y^2}+y\frac{(1-2y)}{2}\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}+\left(y\,nn-mm+\frac14\right)v=0$
$v=\Sigma a_\mu y^\mu\quad\left(\mu(\mu-1)+\frac12\mu-mm+\frac14\right)a_\mu y^\mu$
$-\left(\mu(\mu-1)+\mu-nn\right)a_\mu y^{\mu+1}$
$a_\mu\left(\mu-\frac14+m\right)\left(\mu-\frac14-m\right)=a_{\mu-1}(\mu-1-n)(\mu-1+n)\quad a_\mu=\frac{\Pi(\mu-1-n)\Pi(\mu-1+n)}{\Pi(\mu-\frac14+m)\Pi(\mu-\frac14-m)}y^\mu$

$\varrho^{\frac12}\cos\psi^{\frac12}P\begin{pmatrix}\frac14+m & 0 & n\\ \frac14-m & +\frac12 & -n\end{pmatrix}\cos(\tfrac{\psi}{2})^2\Big)\quad\cos(\tfrac{\psi}{2})^2,\ \sin(\tfrac{\psi}{2})^2,\ -\mathrm{tg}(\tfrac{\psi}{2})^2$

$P\begin{pmatrix}0 & \frac14+m & n\\ +\frac12 & \frac14-m & -n\end{pmatrix}(\sin\tfrac{\psi}{2})^2\Big)=P\begin{pmatrix}\frac14+m & \frac14+m & 2n\\ \frac14-m & \frac14-m & -2n\end{pmatrix}\frac{1-\sin\psi}{2}\Big)$
$=P\begin{pmatrix}0 & n & \frac14+m\\ +\frac12 & -n & \frac14-m\end{pmatrix}-\mathrm{tg}(\tfrac{\psi}{2})^2\Big)=P\begin{pmatrix}[-\frac14+m-] & \frac14+m & \frac{\mathrm{tg}\psi+i}{2i}\\ -n & \frac14-m & \end{pmatrix}\Big)$

$\varrho^{n-\frac12}\frac{\cos}{\sin}m\varphi\,P\begin{pmatrix}m & 0 & n+\frac14\\ -m & +\frac12 & -n+\frac14\end{pmatrix}\cos\psi^2\Big)$

$\int_0^1 y^\alpha(1-y)^\beta(1-xy)^\gamma\partial y=\Sigma\frac{\Pi(n-1-\gamma)\Pi(n+\alpha)}{\Pi n\,\Pi(n+\alpha+\beta+1)}x^n\frac{\Pi\beta}{\Pi-1-\gamma}$
$=\frac{\Pi(\beta)}{\Pi(-1-\gamma)}P\begin{pmatrix}0 & [-x-] & 0 & -\gamma\\ -\alpha+\beta-1 & [-\ldots-] & +\beta+\gamma+1 & \alpha+1\end{pmatrix}x\Big)$
[-$P\begin{pmatrix}m & 0 & n+\frac14\\ -m & \frac12 & -n+\frac14\end{pmatrix}$-]
$\varrho^{n}\frac{\cos}{\sin}m\varphi\,P\begin{pmatrix}m & 0 & n+\frac34\\ -m & \frac12 & -n-\frac14\end{pmatrix}\cos\psi^2\Big)$
$P\begin{pmatrix}n+\frac34 & n+\frac34 & 2m\\ -n-\frac14 & -n-\frac14 & -2m\end{pmatrix}\frac{\mathrm{tg}\psi+i}{2i}\Big)$
$=\left(\frac{\mathrm{tg}\psi+i}{2i}\right)^{n+\frac34}\left(\frac{\mathrm{tg}\psi-i}{-2i}\right)^{-n-\frac14}P\begin{pmatrix}0 & 2n+1 & 2m+\frac12\\ -2n-1 & 0 & -2m+\frac12\end{pmatrix}\frac{1+i\,\mathrm{tg}\psi}{2}\Big)$

$\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\frac{\cos 2m\theta\,\partial\theta}{\sqrt{(z-a)(z'-a')+\left(\frac{z-z'}{2i}\right)^2\sin\theta^2}}=[-\frac{2}{\pi}-]\Sigma\,2\frac{\Pi(n-\frac12)}{\Pi n\,\Pi-\frac12}\frac{(z-z')^{2n}}{(4(z-a)(z'-a'))^{n+\frac12}}\frac{\Pi 2n}{\Pi(n-m)\Pi(n+m)}(-1)^{m+1}2^{-2n+1}$
$=\Sigma_{n,0}\,4\frac{\Pi(n-\frac12)\Pi(n-\frac12)}{\Pi(n-m)\Pi(n+m)}\frac{(z-z')^{2n}}{(4(z-a)(z'-a'))^{n+\frac12}}(-1)^{m+1}\frac{1}{\Pi-\frac12\,\Pi-\frac12}$
$\frac{\Pi 2n}{\Pi n\,\Pi(n-\frac12)}2^{-2n}=\frac{1}{\Pi-\frac12}$

$\int_{z'}^{z}(z-y)^{+2m-\frac12}(z'-y)^{+2m-\frac12}\varphi(y)\partial y(z-z')^{-2m}$
$=\int_0^1(1-y)^{+2m-\frac12}y^{+2m-\frac12}(-1)^{+2m-\frac12}\partial y\,\varphi(z'+(z-z')y)(z-z')^{+2m}$
$(z=z')=\frac{\Pi(2m-\frac12)^2}{\Pi 4m}-i.\,\varphi(z')(z-z')^{2m}$
$\Pi 4m=2^{4m}\Pi(2m)\frac{\Pi(2m-\frac12)}{\Pi-\frac12}$

$\varphi(z)=i.\frac{\Pi(2m-\frac12)^2}{\Pi 4m}=4\frac{\Pi(n-\frac12)^2}{\Pi 2n}\frac{1}{(4(z-a)(z-a'))^{n+\frac12}}(-1)^{m+1}\frac{1}{\Pi-\frac12\,\Pi-\frac12}$
$\varphi_n(y)=\frac{i}{\pi}4\frac{\Pi(n-\frac12)^2}{\Pi 2n}\frac{\Pi 4m\,(-1)^{m+1}}{\Pi(2m-\frac12)^2 4^{m+\frac12}}\frac{1}{((y-a)(y-a'))^{n+\frac12}}$

methods.what: Substitution u = v r^{-1/2} to remove first-derivative term in axisymmetric Laplace equation in cylindrical coordinates
Transformed Laplace equation in complex coordinates z=r+xi, z'=r-xi
Reduction to a hypergeometric-type ODE in y and power series recursion for coefficients
Separated solutions expressed as Riemann P-functions with transformations between arguments
Euler integral representation of hypergeometric series as P-function
Series expansion of a Fourier-cosine integral of inverse square root
Determination of density function φ_n via integral representation
